originalFindingDispositions — complete original3 Evidence findings/subfindings:
E06-01-A / Leave sole Errors with empty caller arrays unchanged: SOURCE-PRESERVED for the precise required actual-Error case. error-ledger.js:88-89 retains the original Error; error-exposure.js:39-54 merely registers an empty secondaryFailures array without appending; error-ledger.js:108-115 refreshes only for multiple entries and :138-145 returns the sole primary without exposure writes. Therefore an Error carrying secondaryFailures=[] retains its own keys, that array reference and the thrown Error reference.
E06-01-B / Deduplicate caller ledger records by identity, not order: PARTIAL / REGRESSED. error-exposure.js:170-173 still uses serialized-object identity, so unrelated caller numeric order collisions do not suppress new diagnostics. Caller array references and existing objects are retained. But Correction09 reconciliation at :95-101 replaces a serialization that recursive ingestion has already appended to the caller array; the outer refresh then appends a second diagnostic for the same occurrence. Finding below gives the exact trigger and repair. Late source/frame/attachment exposure remains connected but cannot be called duplicate-free.
E06-01-C / Ingest genuine failures attached through errorLedger: PARTIAL / REPAIR_REQUIRED. error-exposure.js:7-23,35-37 pre-scans caller wrappers and :73-105 ingests genuine Error references while excluding serialized-only errorLedger diagnostics. The ordinary previously unrecorded ledger-only Error is ingested before later external arrivals. The shared-reference path now obtains wrapper metadata before initial secondary ingestion and does not mutate the caller Error or wrapper. However, re-serialization still lets the Error's own phase override the authoritative wrapper phase, and the replacement creates duplicate exposed diagnostics. Additionally, full chronology across caller collections is not established: :39-54 ingests secondaryFailures before :73-105 processes errorLedger. For primary.secondaryFailures=[b] and primary.errorLedger=[{error:a,phase:'a'},{error:b,phase:'b'}], the chronological common ledger becomes primary,b,a although the caller ledger lists a before b. This is an unresolved original chronological-ingestion obligation, not a claim that every ingestion is broken; reconcile authoritative wrappers and ingest established caller-ledger occurrences before later secondary-only entries without sorting unrelated numeric order namespaces.

findings.body: The frozen09 edit ends the root.evaluate callback with `}, targetCursor)` but removes the closing brace of evaluateActionCandidates before the following exported function. Consequently `export async function evaluateDocumentActivity` is inside an unclosed function body, where an export declaration is syntactically invalid. observation.js imports this module, and both surfaces.js and live-evidence.js transitively import observation.js, so the Evidence partition cannot even be loaded as delivered, independently of its own completed receipt. Frozen08 has the missing function-closing brace. Restore that brace before the next export; this is established by static source comparison, not an executed import failure.
findings.title: Close evaluateActionCandidates before the next export

findings.body: Correction09 removes frozen08's `const serializable = Object.assign({}, packet)` but retains these three uses, and the complete ACTION_RECORDER_INIT_SCRIPT contains no other binding for serializable. On each completed native game action, completePacket marks the event completed and populates the post-handler snapshot, then throws ReferenceError at `delete serializable.root` before publishing a packet or its native-action record. The completedEvents marker also makes document bubbling skip a second completion attempt. evaluateActionCandidates therefore cannot supply the packet consumed by extractActionBracket, executeAction and witness Start; the browser error listener can retain an error event but cannot reconstruct the missing bracket. Restore the copied serializable packet before stripping the live DOM root and publishing it.
findings.title: Restore the serializable packet binding before publication

findings.body: For a primary Error with secondaryFailures=[closeError] and caller errorLedger=[{error:closeError,phase:'close',metadata:{frameUrl:'file:///child.html'}}], recursive recordError(closeError) refreshes the primary's existing caller arrays and appends closeError's serialized object before the outer ingestion reaches this reconciliation branch. Because m is truthy, this branch then replaces existing.serialized even when its phase and metadata already agree. The outer refresh at error-ledger.js:108-115 sees the replacement as a new identity and error-exposure.js:170-173 appends it, leaving two ledger-created diagnostics with the same occurrence/order in the retained caller errorLedger. Internal entries remains deduplicated, but the caller-visible diagnostics used when attachments fail are not. Reconcile the owned serialization in place, or otherwise maintain one stable exposed serialization identity per occurrence without replacing/truncating caller records.
findings.title: Keep the exposed serialization identity stable during reconciliation

findings.body: The new shared-reference reconciliation assigns the authoritative caller-wrapper phase to existing.phase and the old serialized record, but immediately re-serializes the same Error through serializeError, whose error-ledger.js:15 expression is `err?.phase || phase`. With a genuine closeError carrying phase='state' and a caller errorLedger wrapper supplying phase='close' plus frameUrl metadata, getEntries reports the wrapper phase while getSerializedErrors and refreshed exposed diagnostics revert to 'state'. This affects genuine normalized browser Errors too, because materializeEnvelope preserves their phase. The receipt's unconditional authoritative-wrapper phase claim is therefore not supported. Preserve browser intrinsic phase separately if needed, but make the supplied authoritative occurrence phase survive this reconciliation's serialized output without changing the original Error or caller wrapper.
findings.title: Preserve the authoritative wrapper phase in reconciled diagnostics

findings.body: When extractActionBracket has no exact matched packet, its new consumer fallback selects only candidates.find(sequence > cursor.sequence), even though evaluateActionCandidates already returns the entire sequence-eligible candidate collection. If that collection contains multiple observed packet snapshots and a later relevant packet has state/UI getter failures, an outer recorder/document rejection records only the first packet's envelopes and then throws at observation-errors.js:71-72; the later genuine errors never reach the common ledger. Raw staging retains the candidate JSON but does not provide the required normalized chronological occurrences or late thrown exposure. Retain the explicit matched-packet path, and for the rejection/no-match path process the relevant cursor-eligible packets in sequence order before throwing the outer validation failure, rather than collapsing the collection to one packet.
findings.title: Retain all relevant candidate errors before outer rejection
